strong on everything it measured, but it left the wrap mechanism 'unestablished' and shipped a scope boundary (:397 is wrap-insensitive, out of scope) that one command falsified — see the friction record

One command — the --e2e leg P3 never ran — settled the mechanism P3 recorded as unestablished AND falsified a scope boundary P3's premise closure had already signed off. The baseline log shows the Tab walk never reaches the BODY sentinel tabCycleNames() waits on, so both 20-iteration caps exhaust and the walk starts at an arbitrary position: :397 (SC 2.4.3) fails for the same root cause as :384 and its pass on runtime 131 was walk-start luck, not the wrap-insensitivity scope asserted. The ordering is structural, not an oversight: the harness rule puts 'run the leg and read its log' at expect-atom authoring time (P4), while the scope premise closure that the log's content feeds is P3's final step — so a chunk whose leg output bears on a scope premise gets the two steps in the wrong order by construction. Cost: scope.md and research.md each amended mid-P4, and the fix's shape moved from one assertion to the shared walk helper plus both call sites.

step 1 prescribes 'one row per a11y-plan §5 keyboard/focus claim', but §5's run-console-idle bullet bundles TWO SC claims (SC 2.1.1 reachability and SC 2.4.3 order) that are asserted by two DIFFERENT specs — so a bullet-keyed row could name only one of them as its owner, and a claim-keyed row could not be derived from the bullet count alone. Split into two rows rather than inventing a bundled owner, since v3-03's acceptance is quantified over claims and not over bullets
